creative_brief.emotional_promise: Make a first game feel like opening a confident miniature city at dawn: unmistakably Saigon, yet immediately familiar to anyone who knows chess.
creative_brief.format_rationale: A5 is compact enough to live beside the 208 mm board while providing room for a full setup diagram, movement graphics, special rules, troubleshooting, and safety guidance at a legible print scale.
teaching_arc: Recognize the two tactile sides and verify the complete inventory
Match every landmark silhouette to its orthodox chess role
Orient the relief board and build the exact opening position
Move through a guided four-ply opening before independent play
Learn ordinary movement, capture, and all three special moves
Resolve check, checkmate, stalemate, draws, and scoring
Recover from table errors, recount, pack safely, and care for the set
typography: Display and navigation — embedded DejaVu Sans Bold
Body and captions — embedded DejaVu Sans
Landmark labels — embedded DejaVu Sans Oblique
creative_brief.visual_motif: A city-at-first-light system pairs the exact architectural silhouettes with relief-grid geometry, river circles, grid squares, and a low skyline horizon.

findings: The first complete render obscured essential content on pages 3, 5, 8, 9, 11, and 12 through card and callout collisions.
Small body copy and light accent headings reduced print comfort and grayscale contrast on several instructional pages.
The draw card used needlessly restrictive agreement wording for a casual owner manual.
resolved_changes: Reflowed the atlas, four-move walkthrough, special moves, king-safety cards, troubleshooting, and care layouts so every instruction is fully visible.
Increased core body sizes, darkened light-page accents, and verified all twelve revised pages in both color and grayscale at A5 print dimensions.
Simplified the draw card to agreement between the players and removed the final-page skyline that collided with the rules-reference line.
